item.content:encoded:
It was a win-or-go-home game for the Comets, and they live to fight another day after dominating the Aviators in Game 2 of the Championship Series in a 7-2 victory.
Player of the Day
While Zach Ehrhard and James Tibbs III led the way with the bat, it was Landon Knack’s outstanding work as a starter that allowed the Comets to open a five-run lead before the Aviators could think about entering the game. Doing a complete 180 from the previous game’s pitching struggles, Landon Knack didn’t walk anyone and struck out eight in 6.1 one-run innings.
For anyone closely monitoring Knack’s September stats, this was hardly a surprising development, considering he had come into the game with 11.2 scoreless innings this month, 7.2 of them in Triple-A with the Comets.
Triple-A Oklahoma City
The middle-infield combo of Noah Miller and Hyeseong Kim reached in front of Zach Ehrhard in the third inning, and the Comets’ leadoff hitter drove them both in to give his team a lead they would maintain until the end.
Between the third and fifth innings, the Comets scored six of their eventual seven runs, all unanswered, capped by a James Tibbs III three-run bomb, doing what he has done basically the whole year.
The Comets showed discipline to put the ball in play, ending the game with only five strikeouts, under half the total of the Aviators’ lineup. Ryan Fitzgerald, the veteran who was the only Comet to strike out multiple times, got on the scoreboard with a solo shot in the eighth.
Not only dominant, but Knack also found a way to be extremely efficient and could’ve easily gone further than the 6.1 innings he covered, getting the hook when he was at just 81 pitches. Recently demoted flamethrower Seth Halvorsen contributed a scoreless frame with a walk and two strikeouts. The Aviators’ second and final run came against Paul Gervase in the ninth inning.
Transactions
The Comets placed outfielder Chris Newell and pitcher Jackson Ferris on the Development List. The Dodgers optioned pitcher Kyle Hurt and outfielder Josue De Paula to the Comets. Lastly, they activated Emmet Sheehan as well.
Wednesday’s scores
- Las Vegas 2, Oklahoma City 7
Thursday’s schedule
- 7:05 p.m. PT: Oklahoma City (Cole Irvin) at Las Vegas (TBD)

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani got a hit in his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Wednesday night after missing two weeks with right biceps discomfort.
He batted second as the designated hitter against the San Diego Padres and left-handed starter Robbie Ray. Ohtani hits left-handed and throws and pitches right-handed.
“I’m not expecting too much,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s been a while since he’s played, but it’s just good to get him in there.”
A roar went up from Dodger fans as Ohtani walked to the plate to Michael Bublé's “Feeling Good.” He promptly lined a 2-1 pitch from Ray into right field and the fans got loud again. Ohtani was out at second base when Will Smith grounded into a fielder's choice to third.
Mookie Betts was in Ohtani's usual leadoff spot, where he's been since the two-way superstar went on the injured list on Sept. 8.
Betts is hitting .366 with six home runs, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs scored in 18 games in September. He's tied for third in the major leagues with 26 hits this month, and also ranks among National League leaders this month in extra-base hits, RBIs, total bases, doubles and runs.
Ohtani last played on Sept. 7 against Cincinnati and came in hitting .277 with 30 homers, 80 RBIs, 89 runs scored and 80 walks in 134 games. He appeared physically compromised at the plate, shaking out his arm and wincing at times.
Local
Get Los Angeles's latest local news on crime, entertainment, weather, schools, cost of living and more. Here's your go-to source for today's LA news.
“A few weeks ago you could see that he couldn’t hit a fastball, he was underneath everything and it was a slower swing,” Roberts said. “Just controlling the swing, the barrel, I think that’s something I’ll look at and obviously stuff like the wincing, but I don’t expect to see any of that.”
Roberts said he likely would have Ohtani leading off and Betts hitting second against right-handed pitching.
The Dodgers conclude their three-game set against the Padres on Thursday, then head to San Francisco for three games against the Giants to end the regular season.
Roberts expects to see a focused Ohtani at the plate.
“It’s go-time for all of us and I think he’s in a good spot,” Roberts said. “He's getting ready for the postseason. His mind should be there and my bet is that that’s where it’s at.”
In other moves, pitcher Tarik Skubal was reinstated from the bereavement list. He is scheduled to start Friday at San Francisco. Reliever Kyle Hurt was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Rookie Josue De Paula sent back to minors, could return for postseason
With Ohtani's return, Josue De Paula was sent down to Triple-A to join the Comets in the Pacific Coast League playoffs against the Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula had been in the lineup as the DH.
De Paula quickly became a fan favorite during Ohtani's absence. The 21-year-old New York native reached base safely in 10 of his first 11 games in the majors. He went 2 for 3 with a run scored and a walk while notching his first career triple in the Dodgers' 7-0 win over the Padres on Tuesday.
“He performed more than admirably,” Roberts said. “This also just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him.”
If De Paula makes the postseason roster, he would serve as a pinch-hitter.
“Josue has been awesome,” said Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations. “Injected some real life and energy into our team.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — A quad injury cost Jason Adam the chance to help the Padres in last year’s NL Wild Card Series. The team is intent on seeing what the 35-year-old veteran can provide this time around.
Out since late June with a shoulder injury, Adam was activated ahead of Wednesday’s 7:10 p.m. start at Dodger Stadium. To make room, right-hander Griffin Canning was optioned to Triple-A El Paso and reliever Alek Jacob was designated for assignment to allow Adam to rejoin the 40-man roster.
“We saw last year when he got hurt how much we missed him just within the team dynamic and what he provides as experience out there in the bullpen,” Padres manager Craig Stammen said. “We’ve got a lot more experience than what we had last year in the bullpen right now with those guys being together. But Jason’s a big part of that. He’s a big part of that group out there, and then he’s a pretty darn good pitcher also.”
A first-time All-Star last year, Adam allowed nine runs on seven hits and two walks over 1⅓ innings across three rehab appearances with El Paso. But both he and the team were satisfied with the stuff he showed in hitter-friendly conditions, as well as in live batting practice on Monday, and added his experience to a bullpen that was a strength last year and this year.
Adam’s velocity has trended down from about 95 mph the year the Padres acquired him in 2024 (1.95 ERA) to 94 mph last year (1.93 ERA) to 93 mph this year (2.51 ERA). He missed time earlier in the year as he returned from last year’s season-ending quad surgery and said Tuesday he was eager to get back in the thick of a postseason push.
“Yeah, I’d love to be part of every game,” Adam said after joining the team at Dodger Stadium on Tuesday. “What this team’s doing is really special. So I just want to fill my role, however that looks, and help them win ballgames. We’ve seen pretty well that this team’s good with or without me. I just want to do my part to contribute.”
Ousted from the rotation earlier this summer, Canning was better as a reliever (3.82 ERA in 35⅓ innings) than as a starter (6.79 ERA in 50 ⅓ innings) and had been critical in helping the team piece together games ahead of the trade deadline. But the team only needs three starters for the NL Wild Card Series, he was behind the likes of Robbie Ray, Casey Mize and Randy Vásquez in terms of depth arms for a short series and David Morgan has allowed one run in his last 7⅔ innings to seemingly cement his spot in the depth chart ahead of Canning.
The Padres optioning Canning to the minors means he cannot return to the active roster without an injury until the middle of the NL Division Series, after 15 days.
Jacob, 28, had a 5.58 ERA in 61⅓ innings at Triple-A El Paso and 4.18 ERA in 56 innings across parts of four seasons in the majors. He pitched in three games this year, allowing three runs in five innings as an up-and-down arm.
Ohtani returns, Salas starts
As expected the Dodgers reinstated Shohei Ohtani (biceps, knee from the injured list, as well as left-hander Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list. To make room, outfielder Josue De Paula and Hurt were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Ohtani will bat second and serve as the designated hitter for the Dodgers, who have won eight of 11 so far against the Padres this year. Ohtani was 0-for-3 when he last played on Sept. 9 and was in a .122/.295/.184 slide over his last 13 games.
Tonight's #Dodgers lineup vs. Padres: pic.twitter.com/SyL3INJl9z
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 23, 2026
As for the Padres, Ethan Salas will get his first start at Dodger Stadium and second pairing with left-hander Robbie Ray. The only starter he has not worked with is Michael King.
Salas (.627 OPS) was 1-for-2 off the bench on Tuesday. He will bat ninth in a lineup that will see Samad Taylor (.856 OPS) get the start as the DH after Austin Hays did so on Tuesday.
Tonight’s lineup. pic.twitter.com/zLU04b89qh
— San Diego Padres (@Padres) September 23, 2026
While the Padres’ lead on the Diamondbacks was shaved from five to four games with five games left in the season — including three head-to-head matches in San Diego — Tuesday’s loss did little to diminish postseason odds, which are at 93.5% according to FanGraphs.com.
As was the case on Tuesday, any combination of two Padres wins and/or Diamondbacks losses will clinch the team’s third straight postseason berth.
Right-hander Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00 ERA) will start at Coors Field for Arizona against Rockies right-hander Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09 ERA). First pitch there is 5:40 p.m..
The Padres, Cubs and Phillies all began Wednesday with identical 87-70 records, although the Padres have to finish ahead of both teams to earn home games in the NL Wild Card Series as they lost both season series.
The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Braves is 1. They are also one game ahead of the Brewers in the race for the NL’s No. 1 seed.
Glass half full
The Dodgers just about emptied the bullpen in Tuesday’s 7-0 win over the Padres. In the aftermath of another bullpen game slowing an offense that ranks first in the majors this month in OPS (.835), a half-glass-full view of what transpired was worth taking forward.
The Padres saw all but two relievers — Kris Bubic and Evan Phillips — in their first shutout loss since Aug. 25 and they still had two more games to wade through in Chavez Ravine.
“They’re really good bullpen arms, so the more you can see them, the better shot you have,” first baseman Ty France said late Tuesday night. “But just move on to (Wednesday) and try to put some better at-bats together.”
The challenge of a bullpen game is a hitter rarely sees a pitcher twice and the Padres are especially proficient when they see relievers more than once.
They rank 10th in the majors with a .712 OPS against relievers, but 17th the first time they see a reliever (.704) and first the second time they see a reliever (.998 OPS).
Right-hander Kyle Hurt was the only pitcher to finish two innings and he allowed just one hit and faced seven batters while taking down the sixth and seventh innings.
Left-hander Jack Dreyer and right-hander Edwin Diaz got through their frames without giving up a baserunner. The rest of the slate of relievers all faced five batters or less.
In short, things went about as optimal as the Dodgers could hope for from a unit ranks 12th in the majors with a 3.82 ERA.
“The Dodgers bullpen’s got some good arms in it,” Stammen said. “They’re bringing out guys that have really good stuff. But the best way to do it is to play a little small ball and try to beat them that way. We just didn’t have the opportunity to play that way and score one run at a time (after) we get down 4-0. That kind of eliminates that way of playing baseball. But you know, we’ve seen their arms now for the rest of the series, and hopefully that benefits us going forward the next two days.”
Wednesday’s pitching matchup
Padres LHP Robbie Ray (13-8, 3.60 ERA)
He’s got a 5.22 ERA in eight starts since the trade deadline. His last start (6 IP, 3 ER) was one of three quality starts as a Padre and a 6-to-2 strikeout-to-walk ratio was his best since the trade. Ray has a 3.81 ERA in 26 career starts against the Dodgers, but he has allowed 15 earned runs in 19 ⅓ runs over four starts over the last two years.
Here is how Ray has fared against current Dodgers:
Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51 ERA)
He’s thrown a career-high 179 innings while allowing a career-low 5.7 hits per nine innings. His 14 wins are also a new career best. Yamamoto has a 3.76 ERA in seven regular-season starts against the Padres and a 1.35 ERA in three starts this season (20 (IP, 6 BBs, 22 Ks).

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Rested and refreshed, Shohei Ohtani returned to the Dodgers’ roster on Wednesday.
How refreshed remains to be seen.
“These aren’t things that there’s a clear answer to,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani was activated from the injured list before Wednesday’s game. “I think everyone, this time of year, is dealing with some stuff, and so it’s all on that continuum. Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start.
“Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. As they are coming back, it’s important for them to feel that way and when you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’ve done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani is “considerably” closer to being at his best than he was before going on the IL two weeks ago with biceps and knee issues.
“I would say if he was a ‘5’, he’s probably an ‘8’ or a ‘9’ right now,” Roberts said.
He also returned as a ‘2.’
For the first time since Mookie Betts suffered a fractured hand when he was hit by a pitch on June 16, 2024, Roberts wrote Ohtani’s name in as the No. 2 hitter in the Dodgers’ lineup behind Betts.
Roberts said he plans to go with Betts-Ohtani against left-handed pitching (like the Padres’ Wednesday starter, Robbie Ray) and switch to Ohtani-Betts against right-handed pitching (like Thursday’s starter, Nick Pivetta).
“I just feel good about it,” Roberts said of the decision to use both players at leadoff. “It just makes it tougher to navigate versus left(-handed pitching). There’s a Mookie tax. If you want to get to Freddie (Freeman, batting fourth), there’s a Will Smith tax. I like that and versus a right-hander I like kind of flipping those two for the same reasons.”
In four starts as the leadoff hitter before Ohtani returned, Betts was 8 for 16 with four doubles and two home runs.
Overall, the Dodgers went 10-3 in the 13 games Ohtani missed.
SEE YOU SOON
In order to make room for Ohtani on the active roster, rookie outfielder Josue De Paula was sent to Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he made his Triple-A debut Wednesday night in OKC’s playoff game against Las Vegas.
De Paula is expected to rejoin the Dodgers for next week’s bye week and is still in the running for a spot on the postseason roster. Given a “runway” to get at-bats at DH in Ohtani’s absence, De Paula went 10 for 31 (.323) with five extra-base hits (three doubles, a triple and a home run). Perhaps most impressive, he walked 11 times in 42 plate appearances while striking out just five times.
“It was actually an easier conversation than you guys probably would expect, given how well he’s performed,” Roberts said of telling De Paula he was being sent back to the minors – however briefly.
“This was the original thought that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out. We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably.”
By sending De Paula out on Wednesday, he will be eligible to be recalled in time for the first game of a best-of-five National League Division Series next week.
“He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that and that’s what I told him last night,” Roberts said.
Roberts said De Paula showed in his short audition that he is “a special hitter.”
“Doesn’t chase. Moves the ball forward. The threat of power. Lefties don’t faze him,” Roberts recounted. “Hitters don’t (usually) see the ball that quickly out of hand. It’s a gift. No moment is going to be too big for that kid (if he is on the postseason roster).”
PITCHING PLANS
In addition to activating Ohtani on Wednesday, the Dodgers activated starting pitcher Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list and sent right-handed reliever Kyle Hurt back to Triple-A.
Skubal is scheduled to make his final regular-season start on Friday night in San Francisco. Blake Snell came out of his bullpen session on Tuesday with no issues in the groin injury that forced him to leave his start last week after one inning. He is expected to start Saturday’s game in San Francisco as a final test before the postseason.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Nick Pivetta, 3-2, 3.30 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 5-1, 3.46 ERA), Thursday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, TBS, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
Por BETH HARRIS
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani conectó un hit en su regreso a la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles la noche del miércoles, después de perderse dos semanas por molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Bateó segundo como bateador designado contra el abridor zurdo de los Padres de San Diego Robbie Ray.
“No estoy esperando demasiado. Ha pasado un tiempo desde que juega, pero es bueno tenerlo ahí”, comentó el mánager Dave Roberts antes del juego.
Los aficionados ovacionaron a Ohtani cuando caminó hacia el plato con “Feeling Good”, de Michael Bublé. De inmediato conectó una línea al jardín derecho con un lanzamiento de Ray en cuenta de 2-1 y los aficionados volvieron a alborotarse. Ohtani fue puesto out en segunda base cuando Will Smith bateó un rodado para una jugada de selección del fildeador hacia tercera.
Mookie Betts estuvo en el puesto habitual de primer bate de Ohtani, donde ha estado desde que la superestrella ingresó a la lista de lesionados el 8 de septiembre.
Betts batea para .366 con seis jonrones, 21 carreras impulsadas, 13 bases por bolas y 18 carreras anotadas en 18 juegos en septiembre. Está empatado en el tercer lugar de las Grandes Ligas con 26 hits este mes, y también figura entre los líderes de la Liga Nacional este mes en hits de extrabase, carreras impulsadas, bases totales, dobles y carreras anotadas.
Ohtani jugó por última vez el 7 de septiembre contra Cincinnati y llegó bateando para .277 con 30 jonrones, 80 carreras impulsadas, 89 carreras anotadas y 80 bases por bolas en 134 juegos. En el plato se le vio físicamente limitado, sacudiendo el brazo y haciendo gestos de dolor en ocasiones.
“Hace unas semanas se podía ver que no podía batear una recta; se quedaba por debajo de todo y el swing era más lento”, señaló Roberts. “Controlar el swing, el punto de contacto, creo que eso es algo en lo que me fijaré y, obviamente, cosas como los gestos de dolor, pero no espero ver nada de eso”.
Los Dodgers concluyen su serie de tres juegos contra los Padres el jueves, y luego viajan a San Francisco para tres juegos contra los Giants para cerrar la temporada regular.
En otros movimientos, el lanzador Tarik Skubal fue reincorporado desde la lista por duelo. Está programado para abrir el viernes en San Francisco. El relevista Kyle Hurt fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
El novato Josue De Paula fue enviado de vuelta a ligas menores; podría regresar para la postemporada
Con el regreso de Ohtani, Josue De Paula bajó a la Triple-A para unirse a los Comets en los playoffs de la Pacific Coast League contra los Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula había estado en la alineación como bateador designado.
De Paula se convirtió rápidamente en un favorito de los aficionados durante la ausencia de Ohtani. El neoyorquino de 21 años se embasó de manera segura en 10 de sus primeros 11 juegos en las Grandes Ligas. Se fue de 3-2 con una carrera anotada y una base por bolas, mientras conseguía el primer triple de su carrera en la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 sobre los Padres el martes.

LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Wednesday activated Tarik Skubal after the minimum three days on the bereavement list, and optioned Kyle Hurt to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Skubal is scheduled to make his final regular season start on Friday against the San Francisco Giants on the road at Oracle Park. He was placed on bereavement leave on Sunday, which facilitated Emmet Sheehan making a spot appearance before getting optioned himself on Monday.
In nine starts since joining the Dodgers, Skubal has a 2.95 ERA and 3.16 xERA with 60 strikeouts and 13 walks in 55 innings.
Hurt was one of eight Dodgers pitchers to combine for a shut out of San Diego in the series opener on Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium, and the only one to pitch multiple innings. Hurt struck out two in his two scoreless frames on Tuesday, allowing only a single.
In 44 games with the Dodgers this season, Hurt has a 4.14 ERA and 3.76 xERA with 58 strikeouts and 23 walks in 45 2/3 innings. The 28-year-old right-hander recorded his first career save on May 27 against the Colorado Rockies in Los Angeles.

item.content:encoded:
Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs.
This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint.
In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. Shohei Ohtani isn’t pitching, but Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are.
And if all goes according to plan, they will handle the bulk of the innings.
However, replicating the starting pitching excellence of last October won’t be easy. A season ago, the Dodgers’ four-man rotation of Ohtani, Yamamoto, Snell and Glasnow accounted for 113 of the team’s 165 postseason innings (including relief appearances from Glasnow and Yamamoto). Together, they posted a 2.55 ERA.
It was historic production.
Which also means, it’s fair to assume some regression will be possible –– both in workload and effectiveness.
Thus, having more reliable bullpen options this time around could be equally important for the Dodgers. And while that might have felt like a daunting reality earlier this year, when the unit was banged up and struggling through the middle portion of the campaign, Tuesday night was a reminder that the relief corps could be a strength in this fall’s title pursuit.
“Obviously we’ve had a lot of talent over the years,” manager Dave Roberts said. “But as far as sitting here today at the end of the season, it’s as good of shape as we’ve ever been in with the bullpen.”
In a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, the Dodgers were not supposed to have the pitching matchup –– countering Padres ace Michael King with a makeshift bullpen game in a rivalry series opener at Dodger Stadium.
Instead, eight different Dodgers relievers held the previous red-hot Padres to a five-hit shutout. Along the way, several arms who once seemed like question marks continued to round into increasingly promising form.
“It was fantastic,” Roberts said. “This is as good as our bullpen has been, has thrown.”
It started with opener Brock Stewart, a key right-handed weapon in the Dodgers’ bullpen who began the game with a scoreless first inning, continuing his late-season resurgence after another injury-plagued year.
From there, the baton was passed on down.
Justin Wrobleski, who is in the midst of a late-season conversion to the bullpen for the second-straight year, escaped a jam in the second. Blake Treinen, who might be on the postseason roster bubble given the Dodgers’ relief depth, offered one of his best outings of late by issuing only a two-out walk in a scoreless third.

The highlight of the night came in the fourth and fifth, when Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz hung a couple more zeroes in what were important appearances from each.
For Sasaki, the outing marked his first since returning from the injured list and making his own late-season move back to the bullpen, where he could reprise his role as closer from last year’s playoffs. He worked around a pair of singles with two strikeouts and a fastball that, even after being sidelined for the last month by a blister, sat at 99-100 mph.
For Díaz, Tuesday was not only a third-consecutive scoreless outing since his own return from the IL, but his most impressive yet as he makes a bid for the playoff roster. He retired the top of the Padres lineup in order with a pair of strikeouts, and has now retired 9 of 11 batters he has faced since rejoining the active roster.
Asked postgame if Díaz –– the $69 million offseason signing who lost the closer’s job amid a previously dismal debut Dodgers season –– could still pitch his way back into ninth-inning duties, Roberts said it’s “certainly possible.”
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” Roberts added.
By that point, the Dodgers had already pulled away from the Padres. They mounted a four-run rally with two outs in the second against King, who issued back-to-back bases-loaded walks to Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts before Freddie Freeman slashed a two-run single through the infield. The offense tacked on more runs in the fourth (on another Freeman RBI single), the sixth (on a solo home run from Tommy Edman), and the seventh (a Will Smith solo blast).
In what was the lineup’s toughest test in a while, they passed with flying colors.
Still, the night’s most encouraging developments came from the ‘pen, which capped off the game with two scoreless innings from Kyle Hurt, then stress-free appearances in the eighth and ninth from Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer.
The unit’s most trusted arms at the moment, Tanner Scott (who figures to be vying with Sasaki for the postseason closer role) and Evan Phillips, weren’t even required. Nor was Edgardo Henriquez, who remains sidelined by a back injury but still could return in time for the playoffs.
“We know we have a good group, and anytime we get to carry the load and everybody has success and throws up zeros, it’s special,” Stewart said. “That’s really hard to do, for all eight guys or whatever it was today. So yeah, it’s cool.”
With a smirk, he added: “Write stories about it.”
Come October, of course, the Dodgers will be hoping their relievers are the main story.
But if the rotation falters, the club seems significantly better-suited to handle it than it did a year ago.
“That could change in a day, in a game, as we all know,” Roberts said. “But right now, feel really good about everyone out there.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium.
With the win, the Dodgers are up five games on the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League playoffs, with five games remaining in the regular season. The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a bye into the NLDS is down to just one.
King hadn’t allowed more than three runs in any of his previous nine starts, with a 2.26 ERA during that span, and he retired his first five batters faced on Tuesday. Then with two outs in the second inning, the next six batters reached, breaking open the scoring.
Teoscar Hernández singles for the Dodgers’ first hit, then Josue De Paula singled on an 0-2 pitch before Andy Pages was hit by a pitch in his very first plate appearance back since getting hit by a pitch one month prior, to load the bases. Tommy Edman walked on four pitches for the game’s first run, Mookie Betts only needed five pitches to walk home another run, then Freddie Freeman grounded a single through the infield, and under the legs of a leaping Edman, to score two more.
Betts hit a ground-rule double in the fourth, followed by another RBI single by Freeman for a fifth run against King.
Solo home runs by Edman in the sixth and Will Smith in the seventh off the Padres bullpen padded the scoring.
With Emmet Sheehan optioned on Tuesday and Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, the Dodgers have only three active pitchers they plan to use as starting pitchers in the postseason at the moment. That means they have 11 relievers, and on a day following an off day and the day before a start by the MLB leader in innings per start, the Dodgers used .. pitchers to cover the nine innings.
Starters Justin Wrobleski and Roki Sasaki — the latter just activated on Tuesday — each pitched only one inning, both scoreless. Sasaki was hitting 100 mph in his first game action in four weeks.
Kyle Hurt was the only Dodgers pitcher to toss more than one inning, taking care of the sixth and seventh.
Jack Dreyer was the first pitcher of Sunday’s game, and the last pitcher on Tuesday.
It’s only the third time in franchise history the Dodgers used eight pitchers in a shutout of no more than nine innings, done also on September 29, 2019 in San Francisco and May 15 this year in Anaheim. For some perspective, when the Dodgers beat the Expos 1-0 Montreal in 22 innings on August 23, 1989 — Rick Dempsey homered, Tommy Lasorda got Expos mascot Youppi ejected — the Dodgers only used five pitchers that day.
Tuesday particulars
Home runs: Tommy Edman (8), Will Smith (10)
WP — Justin Wrobleski (12-5): 1 IP, 1 hit
LP — Michael King (12-10): 4 IP, 6 hits, 5 runs, 2 walks, 5 strikeouts
